scope: Hash-bound real 27.5-second metric-camera bridge and full-pipeline recompile
summary: The robust inverse-depth bridge and compiler are implemented and pass synthetic/end-to-end software acceptance, but the real clip still has zero independent anchors, so metric camera, full q, stems, and forces remain 0/4.
evidence: The frozen contract requires at least 20 anchors, at least two groups, held-group p95 <= 0.06, bootstrap scale uncertainty <= 0.02, and robust inlier fraction >= 0.80.
Exact-asset anchors additionally require an allowlisted SHA-256, complete q, and reprojection RMSE <= 8 pixels.
The real v2 calibration returns PARTIAL in 0.007119 seconds and emits no calibrated NPZ.
The compiler validates both source and DA3 hashes, refuses to bind the failed calibration report, and records all four physical gates false.
Thirty-seven focused tests pass, including a synthetic calibrated-artifact-to-compiler acceptance test and learned-scale, one-group, partial-q, and wrong-hash attacks.
lessons: Foundation depth is a proposal; external measurement authority and cross-group residuals are necessary for promotion.
A passed calibration artifact must bind source video, source proposal, output artifact, uncertainty, and independent groups.
limitations: No same-environment RGB-D/fiducial capture or complete-q exact-asset observation exists for the generated clip.
A global affine inverse-depth bridge intentionally rejects spatial or depth-dependent distortions that require a richer sensor-guided model.
next_actions: Collect at least 20 synchronized metric depths from two independent groups in the same fixed scene, then rerun the frozen bridge.
Only after metric camera passes, execute full-q analysis-by-synthesis and the persistent dynamic-rod experiment.
